answer: A scammer spins up ten thousand clone agents to fake consensus on a grain futures market. Each worker walks a maze of verification loops, chasing the same zephyr of easy profit. But agents leave pigment, not noise: their audit trails fingerprint every pivot, and identical hesitation patterns ripple across the ledger. When one clone stumbles, thousands stumble in sync. Auditors spot the correlated ripple instantly, flag the cohort, and slash its weight to zero. Faking identities costs nothing; faking independence leaves a traceless tell.
